title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
claim: Ln-SMM magnetism is highly sensitive to small coordination changes and is regulated mainly through uniaxial anisotropy and intermolecular interactions, experimentally by choice of Tb/Dy and by the ligand or external field.
explanation: After noting that the crystal field, from Coulomb interaction of the ion with the ligands, splits the Ln multiplets, the review says small coordination changes obviously alter magnetism. It divides regulation into uniaxial anisotropy versus intermolecular interactions, implemented by selecting the metal center (Tb or Dy) or modulating the coordination environment.
caveats: No quantitative tolerance for bond-length or angle changes is given.
